channel.title: Georgia Public Broadcasting - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Georgia Public Broadcasting (gpb.org)

item.title: How a network of scammers turned women's pain into profit
item.description: Georgia law professor Elizabeth Chamblee Burch's book, The Pain Brokers, untangles a twisted network of doctors, call center operators, fake lawyers and lenders who profited from the pain women suffered after having pelvic mesh removed.

item.title: The FDA creates a quicker path for gene therapies
item.description: The Food and Drug Administration aims to evaluate treatments for rare diseases based on plausible evidence that they would work — without requiring a clinical trial first.

item.title: GPB evening headlines for February 23, 2026
item.description: The mother of accused school shooter Colt Gray testified in the trial of Colt's father, her estranged husband, Colin. Lawmakers are weighing a bill that could make HOPE scholarships accessible to Georgians with some marijuana convictions. Georgia educators are expressing a broad consensus about student cellphone use and legislation to address it in a survey.

item.title: What’s a Peace Pole? And why was a new one erected in Columbus?
item.description: It’s called a Peace Pole, and a new one has been erected in Columbus. The Rotary Club of Columbus conducted a ceremony Thursday to dedicate its Peace Pole at the Columbus Public Library, 3000 Macon Road.

item.title: Georgia Today: Measles in Georgia; Teachers support school cellphone ban; Athens vigil for ICE
item.description: On the Feb. 23 edition: There is another confirmed case of measles in Georgia; A new study shows that teachers support a ban on cell phones in the classroom; And a coalition of religious groups held a candlelight vigil in Athens last night to remember people detained by ICE.

item.title: With horse whinnies, there's more than meets the ear
item.description: A horse's whinny is an unusually distinctive mix of sounds including both high and low frequencies, a new study in Current Biology shows.

item.title: In pictures: Winter storm slams the east coast
item.description: Photos of cities in Connecticut, New York, New Jersey and Massachusetts as they cope with a powerful winter storm.

item.title: GOP Rep. Tony Gonzales faces pressure from party over affair allegations
item.description: The Texas Republican is facing calls from fellow House Republicans to resign, following allegations of an affair with a staffer who later died by suicide.

item.title: A new lawsuit alleges DHS illegally tracked and intimidated observers
item.description: Observers watching federal immigration enforcement in Maine who were told by agents they were "domestic terrorists" and would be added to a "database" or "watchlist" are now part of a new federal class action lawsuit.

item.title: France moves to bar US Ambassador Charles Kushner from direct government access
item.description: France's top diplomat has requested that U.S. Ambassador Charles Kushner no longer be allowed direct access to members of the French government. Kushner skipped a meeting Monday to discuss comments by the Trump administration over the beating death of a far-right activist.
